description: English text (Current Chinese Braille convention for embedded English): the first letter of a word carries a case sign, the rest are bare. Inside a running English stretch the lowercase sign ⠰ is dropped on following lowercase words — it only announces 'a Latin letter starts here', redundant once English is already underway — so a whole sentence shows it at most once. The capital sign keeps emitting per word because it carries case (World vs world).

lower_word.description: Lowercase word — one lowercase sign + bare letters

mixed_case.description: Mixed case — the first letter's case picks the sign, subsequent letters are bare

cases.note: two capitalized words — the capital sign is per-word (it carries case), so World keeps its ⠠

acronym.description: All-caps acronym — whole-word capitals double the upper sign (⠠⠠) + bare letters; a single ⠠ means only the first letter is capital

running_english.description: A running stretch of English: the lowercase sign ⠰ appears at most once (on the first word, and only if it's lowercase), then following lowercase words run bare. Spaces, punctuation and digits don't break the run; Chinese does. Capitals keep their per-word sign throughout. A digit run re-arms the sign: bare a–j cells ARE digit cells, so a word right after digits re-announces ⠰ (42 abc would otherwise read its a as another digit).

cases.note: sign once on hello; world runs bare
capital opens the run; world bare
whole sentence: one capital sign up front, no signs after
the takes ⠰; CPU keeps its doubled capital sign; is / fast run bare
the digit run (⠼…) carries the English context across, but re-arms the lowercase sign: bare d IS the digit-4 cell, so def re-announces ⠰
a word glued right after digits re-signs too — bare f IS the digit-6 cell (used to read 326…)

dotted_abbrev.description: Abbreviation with periods. The period carries the English run (it doesn't break it), so only the first letter takes the lowercase sign and the second runs bare. An English '.' is followed by one blank.

cases.note: i takes ⠰; the period carries the run; e runs bare; each period adds a blank
e takes ⠰; g runs bare after the carrying period
